channel.title: Benjamin Yi — Writing & Research
channel.description: Essays and research papers by Benjamin Yi (Ben Yi) on thermodynamic computing, physics-optimal AI architectures, and complex systems.

item.title: The Point Was Always to Be Outgrown
item.description: On AI, fear, and the oldest hope a parent has. Every generation was allowed to become more capable than the one before; AI is the first child the whole species has raised together.

item.title: You Cannot Hire Your Way Out of a Systems Problem
item.description: Contractors are run correctly, on the wrong architecture. The trades were never the bottleneck; the manual synchronization layer above them was.

item.title: Scale Invariance in Construction Software
item.description: One recursive project type for every site, building, and unit. Borrowing the renormalization group so features, rollups, and new scales hold by construction.

item.title: Beyond Transformers: Toward Physics-Optimal Architectures for Large Language Models
item.description: The transformer is a local optimum constrained by deterministic silicon. A first-principles framework built on attractor dynamics, phase-synchronization attention, and complete thought-states.

item.title: Continuous Thermodynamic Descent: A Non-Equilibrium Training Algorithm for Thermodynamic Stochastic Hardware
item.description: Training without backpropagation: deposition, erosion, and weathering continuously sculpt an energy landscape in perpetual non-equilibrium.
